name: Gaussian-prime paths with small maximum jumps
description: construct() -> a list of distinct integer coordinate pairs in [-64,64]^2, starting at (1,1), ending with max(abs(x),abs(y))>=50, and containing only Gaussian primes. Minimize the largest squared Euclidean step. Axis primes must be 3 modulo 4; off-axis norms must be prime. The finite path minimizes its largest jump inside a bounded square; it does not establish an infinite path or reproduce the periodic-moat proof. The optimum is 8, found by breadth-first search over all Gaussian primes in the box; this is a rediscovery task.

limitations: Solved finite case: With steps of squared length at most 5, the Gaussian primes reachable from 1+i stay inside max(|x|,|y|) < 50, while squared length 8 suffices.
The finite endpoint and coordinate bounds cannot resolve the infinite Gaussian moat problem. The elementary two-point starter is locally chosen, not a published record.

state_of_the_art.statement: With steps of squared length at most 5, the Gaussian primes reachable from 1+i stay inside max(|x|,|y|) < 50, while squared length 8 suffices. A breadth-first search over all Gaussian primes in [-64,64]^2 (scripts/check_state_of_the_art.py) gives the optimum 8. Whether a walk with bounded steps can reach infinity is the Gaussian moat problem (Erdős Problem #952).
